text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure is considered high when it is consistently 130/80 mm Hg or higher, according to guidelines from the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure readings use two numbers:

list.snippet: Systolic (top number): Measures pressure in your arteries when your heart beats.
Diastolic (bottom number): Measures pressure in your arteries when your heart rests between beats.
Elevated: Systolic between 120–129 and diastolic less than 80 mm Hg
Stage 1 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): Systolic 130–139 or diastolic 80–89 mm Hg
Stage 2 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): Systolic 140 or higher or diastolic 90 or higher mm Hg
Severe Hypertension / Hypertensive Crisis: Systolic higher than 180 and/or diastolic higher than 120 mm Hg

If it is higher than 180/120 mm Hg with symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, or vision changes, it is a hypertensive emergency requiring a call to 911 immediately.
